svg.text: Intelligent Suspension System - HTS interlock controller
Electrical schematic redrawn from the project drawing (Schema_elettrico.pdf). Pin map matches Main_Control_Logic.ino v2.0.
Red wires = power distribution, green wires = signals. The Arduino is powered by the L298N.
1. D2 reaches the pull-up board in the drawing and no buzzer is drawn. The firmware drives the buzzer on D2: confirm where it is connected.
2. R1 is 120 ohm in the drawing. If it is really 120 kohm the value must be corrected here and in the signal-range check on A10.
3. L298N: in the drawing D10 and D11 land on the first and third pins of the 6-pin header. Drawn here as IN1/IN2: confirm pins and ENA jumper.
4. U3: as drawn, the orange wire goes to the terminal marked GND and VCC is on the battery line; output + is unconnected. Verify with a multimeter.
5. The Arduino VIN is fed by the 5 V terminal of the L298N. VIN normally expects 7-12 V: measure the 5V pin of the Arduino under load.
6. Connectors J1-J5 are mating pairs (plug and socket). Small grey codes give the wire colours of the drawing.
